description: Statements a report might make about the Larkholm sources, each with the documents it cites and a gold support level read from those documents. 'supported' means the cited text states it; 'partial' means part of it is stated and part is not; 'unsupported' means a figure is wrong, or the text does not state it, or the text says otherwise. Several 'unsupported' and 'partial' items reuse the sources' own words on purpose: they are the cases a word-overlap check is expected to get wrong.

claims.text: Council counts show 412,000 one-way crossings in 2025.
The battery-electric replacement would cost $14.2 million.
The Clean Coasts Fund would pay 40% of the electric vessel's cost if the Council commits before 30 September.
71% of respondents oppose a reduced winter timetable.
The operator proposes four daily return sailings in winter instead of six.
Grid upgrades for charging are expected to take 14 to 18 months.
The Finance Committee will not raise the annual ferry subsidy above $1.8 million.
Visitors account for about 70% of summer crossings.
The Health Centre reports about 140 patient trips a month to mainland clinics between November and March.
The Residents' Association asks the Council to cap any fare increase at 5%.
Council counts show 450,000 one-way crossings in 2025.
The battery-electric replacement would cost $12.4 million.
The Clean Coasts Fund would pay 60% of the electric vessel's cost if the Council commits before 30 September.
85% of respondents oppose a reduced winter timetable.
The Council has approved the electric ferry and signed the vessel contract.
The operator guarantees that no winter sailings will be cancelled in storms.
The Residents' Association will oppose an electric ferry under any conditions.
The Green Tide Alliance polled 4,000 visitors and residents.
The operator proposes a 12% fare increase and a free bus link to the ferry terminal.
The grant deadline is 30 September, and the grant covers the full cost of the vessel.
The diesel refit costs $3.1 million and would extend the vessel's life by about twenty years.
The Association surveyed 1,150 households and every household replied.
